title: 3Sum
corePattern: Sorting + Fix-One-Element Reduction to 2Sum with Two Pointers
interviewTips: Clarify: should output unique triplets only, order of triplets and numbers inside does not matter, and how to handle fewer than 3 elements?
Trade-off: brute force O(n^3) vs hashmap O(n^2) time + O(n) space vs sorted two-pointers O(n^2) time + O(1) extra space - sorting enables O(1) duplicate skipping.
Edge-case tip: explicitly discuss duplicate skipping for i, left and right pointers, early break when nums[i] > 0, and all-zeros input [0,0,0,0].
Complexity tip: sorting dominates setup O(n log n), then outer loop O(n) * inner two-pointer O(n) = O(n^2) total; state that output size can be O(n^2) in worst case.

approaches.name: Approach 1: Brute Force with Sorting for Deduplication
approaches.intuition: Try every triplet i < j < k, check if sum is zero, and deduplicate by sorting each found triplet and storing in a set.
approaches.theory: There are C(n,3) = O(n^3) triplets. For each we do O(1) sum check and O(1) sort of 3 elements. Canonical sorted form ensures [-1,0,1] and [0,-1,1] map to same key, so a hash set removes duplicates. Finally convert set to list.

timeComplexity.explanation: Triple nested loops enumerate O(n^3) triplets, each sum check and 3-element sort is O(1).

spaceComplexity.explanation: Extra space for set of unique triplets where k is number of unique triplets; sorting triplet is O(1). Excluding output, O(k) for deduplication.

steps: Continue all C(6,3)=20 combos, set dedupes duplicate [-1,0,1]

edgeCases: All zeros [0,0,0,0]: single triplet [0,0,0] after dedup
Heavy duplicates e.g. [-2,-2,0,0,2,2]: set prevents duplicate outputs

approaches.name: Approach 2: Sort + Fix First + HashSet for 2Sum
approaches.intuition: Sort to handle duplicates easily, fix nums[i] as first element, then solve 2Sum for target = -nums[i] on suffix using a hash set in one pass.
approaches.theory: After sorting, outer loop fixes i and skips duplicate nums[i]. For each i, scan j > i maintaining seen set of values. Complement = -nums[i]-nums[j]; if complement in seen, we found a triplet. Skip duplicate j values after a hit to keep uniqueness. Sorting makes duplicate skipping O(1) and guarantees canonical order nums[i] <= complement <= nums[j] when found via prior seen elements.

timeComplexity.explanation: Sorting O(n log n) + outer loop O(n) * inner scan O(n) with O(1) hash ops = O(n^2) total.

spaceComplexity.explanation: O(n) for hash set per outer iteration (reused) plus O(log n) to O(n) for sort depending on implementation; output excluded.

steps: i=0 val -4: seen={}, scan j=1..5, no complement match -> no triplet
i=1 val -1: seen={}: j=2(-1) comp=2 not in seen, seen={-1}; j=3(0) comp=1 not in seen, seen={-1,0}; j=4(1) comp=0 in seen -> add [-1,0,1]; j=5(2) comp=-1 in seen -> add [-1,-1,2]
i=2 val -1 duplicate of i=1 -> skip
i=3 val 0: scan remainder finds nothing

edgeCases: Duplicate i values: skip to avoid duplicate triplets
Duplicate j values: skip forward after hit
Target overflow: in Java/C++ use long or careful int range; Python unbounded
[0,0,0,0]: i=0 finds [0,0,0], i>=1 skipped as duplicates

approaches.name: Approach 3: Sort + Two Pointers
approaches.intuition: Sort the array, fix one index i, then use left/right pointers moving toward each other to find pairs summing to -nums[i] in linear time.
approaches.theory: Sorting enables the classic 2Sum-II two-pointer technique: for fixed i, if nums[i]+nums[l]+nums[r] < 0 need larger sum so l++, if > 0 need smaller sum so r--, if ==0 record and move both while skipping duplicates. Skipping duplicate i and duplicate l/r guarantees uniqueness. Early break when nums[i] > 0 because sorted suffix cannot sum to zero.

timeComplexity.explanation: Sorting O(n log n) + for each of O(n) fixed i, two-pointer scan is O(n) worst case, total O(n^2).

spaceComplexity.complexity: O(1) extra, O(log n) to O(n) with sort
spaceComplexity.explanation: Only constant pointers besides output; sorting uses O(log n) stack in Java/Python or O(log n) introsort in C++; output space excluded, otherwise O(k) for results.

steps: i=2 (-1) duplicate -> skip, i=3 (0): l=4(1) r=5(2) s=3 >0 -> r-- until l>=r

edgeCases: n < 3: loop does not run, return []
nums[i] > 0: break early, remaining triplets all positive
All zeros [0,0,0]: l/r dedup leaves single [0,0,0]
Integer overflow in C++/Java when summing: values within [-1e5,1e5] safe in int, but use long if constraints larger
